about: Base texts for independence-pairs-v1.jsonl. Written by hand for this eval on 2026-10-18; every text is original and the three texts of a topic were written independently of each other (different structure, wording and emphasis), so a pair of them is an independent pair by construction. Translations are translations of the English text named in `translation_of`. build_independence_pairs.py derives every pair from these texts.

docs.text: Python's asyncio module runs coroutines on a single-threaded event loop. A coroutine is declared with async def and suspends itself at every await expression, handing control back to the loop so that another task can make progress. Because only one task runs at a time, asyncio suits programs that spend most of their time waiting on sockets, pipes or timers rather than computing. CPU-heavy work still blocks the loop; the documentation recommends moving it to a thread or process pool with run_in_executor. Tasks are created with asyncio.create_task, and asyncio.gather waits for several of them while collecting their results in order. Cancellation is delivered as a CancelledError raised at the next await point inside the cancelled task.

When I first moved a web scraper to asyncio I expected everything to get faster, and at first nothing did. The reason was a single call to time.sleep buried in a helper: one blocking call freezes the whole event loop, because every coroutine shares the same thread. Swapping it for await asyncio.sleep fixed the stall immediately. The other lesson was that concurrency needs limits. Launching ten thousand requests at once exhausted file descriptors, so I wrapped each fetch in an asyncio.Semaphore with a small count. Finally, I learned to keep references to background tasks, since a task object that nothing refers to can be garbage collected before it finishes its work.

Structured concurrency arrived in the standard library with TaskGroup in Python 3.11. Inside an async with block, every task started through the group is awaited when the block exits, and if one child raises, the remaining children are cancelled and the errors are reported together as an ExceptionGroup. This replaces many hand-written patterns built on gather with return_exceptions set to true. Timeouts follow the same idea: asyncio.timeout is a context manager that cancels the enclosed work when the deadline passes and converts the cancellation into TimeoutError at the boundary. Together these tools make the lifetime of concurrent work visible in the shape of the code instead of scattered across callbacks.

HTTP caches decide whether a stored response may be reused by reading the Cache-Control header. The max-age directive gives the number of seconds a response stays fresh; once that time has passed the cache must revalidate it with the origin server before serving it again. Revalidation is cheap when the response carried a validator. An ETag is an opaque version identifier, and a conditional request with If-None-Match lets the server answer 304 Not Modified without sending the body again. The no-store directive forbids storing the response at all, while no-cache allows storage but requires revalidation on every use. Shared caches such as CDNs also honour s-maxage, which overrides max-age for them only.

Our dashboard kept showing yesterday's numbers to some customers, and the culprit turned out to be a proxy in their corporate network. We had sent the API responses without any caching headers, so the proxy fell back on heuristic freshness and kept them for hours. The fix was to be explicit. Personalised responses now carry Cache-Control private, which keeps them out of shared caches entirely, and the static bundles carry a content hash in the file name together with a one year lifetime and the immutable flag. Since that change, deploys reach every user on the next page load, and the bandwidth bill went down because the bundles are almost never downloaded twice.

The Vary header tells a cache which request headers were used to choose the response. A server that returns compressed or uncompressed bodies depending on Accept-Encoding must send Vary Accept-Encoding, otherwise a cache may hand a gzip body to a client that cannot decode it. Varying on headers with many distinct values, such as User-Agent or Cookie, fragments the cache into thousands of entries and destroys the hit rate. Content delivery networks therefore normalise those headers or ignore them, and many offer a separate cache key configuration instead. A related directive, stale-while-revalidate, lets a cache serve an expired response for a short window while it fetches a fresh copy in the background.

Every value in Rust has a single owner, the variable that holds it, and the value is dropped when its owner goes out of scope. Assigning a heap-allocated value such as a String to another variable moves ownership, after which the original variable can no longer be used. Types that implement the Copy trait, like integers and booleans, are duplicated instead of moved. To use a value without taking ownership, code borrows it through a reference. Any number of shared references may exist at once, or exactly one mutable reference, but never both at the same time. The borrow checker enforces these rules at compile time, which removes data races and use-after-free errors without a garbage collector.

Coming from Java, the error message I saw most in my first month of Rust was cannot borrow as mutable because it is also borrowed as immutable. It usually appeared when I held a reference into a vector and then tried to push onto the same vector. Pushing may reallocate the buffer and leave the reference dangling, so the compiler refuses. Rewriting the loop to collect indices first, or cloning the small piece of data I needed, made the error disappear. Lifetimes felt abstract until I read them as a promise: the returned reference lives no longer than the input it was taken from. After that the annotations stopped looking like noise.

Interior mutability is the escape hatch for cases the borrow checker cannot verify statically. RefCell moves the shared-or-exclusive rule from compile time to run time: borrow and borrow_mut hand out guards and panic if the rule would be broken. Combined with Rc, it allows several owners to mutate a shared value in single-threaded code, for example the nodes of a graph. Across threads the equivalents are Arc for shared ownership and Mutex or RwLock for synchronised access. Cell is a lighter tool for Copy types that replaces the whole value rather than lending references. These types do not weaken the guarantees; they check the same invariants at a different time.

High blood pressure rarely causes symptoms, which is why it is often found only during a routine check. A reading has two numbers: systolic pressure while the heart beats and diastolic pressure between beats. Many guidelines define hypertension as a sustained reading of 140 over 90 millimetres of mercury or higher, although some lower the threshold to 130 over 80. Diagnosis should rest on several readings taken on different days, ideally including measurements at home, because a single high value in a clinic can reflect anxiety. Untreated, raised pressure damages arteries over years and increases the risk of stroke, heart attack and kidney disease.

Lifestyle changes lower blood pressure in a measurable way. Cutting salt intake has one of the largest effects, especially for people who eat a lot of processed food, where most dietary sodium hides. Regular aerobic exercise, such as brisk walking on most days of the week, reduces systolic pressure by several points. Losing excess weight, limiting alcohol and eating more vegetables, fruit and low-fat dairy all add to the benefit, and the DASH eating plan was designed around exactly these foods. When changes are not enough, doctors usually start with one of a few drug classes, including thiazide diuretics, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers and calcium channel blockers.

My father's cuff at home showed numbers far lower than the ones his doctor recorded, and for a while we suspected the device. The nurse explained that technique matters more than the brand. He had been measuring right after climbing the stairs, with his arm hanging down and the cuff over his sleeve. Sitting quietly for five minutes, resting the arm on a table at heart level and placing the cuff on bare skin brought the home readings close to the clinic ones. She also suggested taking two readings a minute apart, morning and evening for a week, and bringing the written log rather than remembering a single figure.

Vitamin D is made in the skin when ultraviolet B light from the sun strikes it, and smaller amounts come from oily fish, egg yolks and fortified foods. The body converts it in the liver and then the kidneys into its active hormone form, which helps the intestine absorb calcium and phosphate. Severe deficiency causes rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults, conditions in which bones soften and deform. People who spend little time outdoors, have darker skin or live at high latitudes are more likely to be low, especially in winter. Blood levels are usually assessed by measuring 25-hydroxyvitamin D, the main circulating form.

Large randomised trials have tempered the enthusiasm for vitamin D supplements. In studies that gave thousands of healthy adults daily doses for several years, the supplement did not reduce the rate of cancer, cardiovascular events or fractures compared with placebo in people who were not deficient to begin with. The picture is different for people with confirmed deficiency, for older adults in care homes who rarely go outside, and for infants who are exclusively breastfed, where supplementation is commonly advised. Very high doses taken for long periods can raise blood calcium to harmful levels, so more is not automatically better, and testing before high-dose treatment is sensible.

Every October our family switches to the winter routine our paediatrician suggested: one small drop of vitamin D for the toddler with breakfast and a tablet for the adults. Living this far north, she said, the sun is simply too low between late autumn and early spring for the skin to make much, no matter how long the children play outside. I keep the bottle next to the cereal so nobody forgets. She warned us not to double up with a multivitamin that already contains it and to keep the drops out of reach, since the concentrated liquid is easy to overdose on. In April, when the days are long again, we stop.

Article 17 of the General Data Protection Regulation gives a person the right to have personal data about them erased without undue delay. The right applies on specific grounds, among them that the data are no longer necessary for the purpose they were collected for, that the person withdraws the consent the processing relied on, or that the data were processed unlawfully. It is not absolute. A controller may refuse erasure where processing is needed for freedom of expression, to comply with a legal obligation, for reasons of public health, for archiving in the public interest or to establish and defend legal claims. Where data were made public, reasonable steps must be taken to inform other controllers.

Handling deletion requests at a mid-sized online shop taught us that the hard part is finding the data, not deleting it. A customer's details lived in the order database, the newsletter tool, the support desk, the analytics warehouse and three years of nightly backups. We built an inventory first, then a script that removes or anonymises the customer in every live system within a month of the request. Order records needed for tax law are kept but cut down to the minimum. Backups are not edited; instead, a suppression list makes sure deleted customers are removed again if a backup is ever restored. Each request and its completion date go into a log.

The so-called right to be forgotten predates the regulation. In its 2014 Google Spain judgment the Court of Justice of the European Union held that a search engine is responsible for the processing it carries out and must, on request, remove links to pages about a person when the information is inadequate, irrelevant or excessive, unless the public interest in finding it prevails. A later judgment limited the obligation to search results shown in the member states rather than worldwide. Search engines now publish transparency reports listing how many delisting requests they receive and the share they grant, which has hovered around half of the URLs evaluated.

United States copyright law permits fair use of protected works without the owner's permission, and section 107 of the Copyright Act lists four factors that courts weigh. The first is the purpose and character of the use, including whether it is commercial and whether it transforms the original by adding new expression or meaning. The second is the nature of the copyrighted work, with factual works receiving thinner protection than creative ones. The third is the amount and substantiality of the portion taken. The fourth is the effect of the use on the potential market for the original. No single factor decides a case, and the outcome depends heavily on the facts.

As a video essayist I live inside the fair use grey zone. My rule of thumb is to use clips only as evidence for an argument I am making out loud, never as entertainment on their own. I keep each excerpt as short as the point requires, talk over it or pause it to annotate, and avoid the climactic scenes that people would otherwise pay to see. None of this guarantees anything, and an automated claim can still demonetise a video within minutes of upload. When that happens I dispute it with a written explanation of the commentary, and in most cases the claim has been released after a review by a person.

The Supreme Court's 2023 decision in Andy Warhol Foundation v. Goldsmith narrowed how far transformation can carry a fair use defence. The case concerned an orange silkscreen based on Lynn Goldsmith's photograph of Prince, licensed to a magazine for a cover. The majority held that, for that specific use, the first factor favoured Goldsmith because the licence served substantially the same commercial purpose as her own licensing of the photograph. A new aesthetic or message was not enough on its own. Commentators have read the opinion as asking courts to look at the particular use being challenged rather than at the artwork in the abstract.

The Peace of Westphalia is the name given to the treaties signed in the cities of Osnabrück and Münster in 1648, which ended the Thirty Years' War in the Holy Roman Empire and the Eighty Years' War between Spain and the Dutch Republic. Negotiations had dragged on for several years, with delegations from across Europe lodged in the two towns. The settlement confirmed the right of the princes of the Empire to conduct their own foreign policy within limits, extended the religious compromise of 1555 to Calvinists, and recognised the independence of the Dutch Republic and the Swiss Confederation. Sweden and France gained territory along the Baltic and the Rhine.

Political scientists often call the modern international order Westphalian, meaning a system of sovereign states that do not interfere in each other's internal affairs. Historians have pushed back on that label. The treaties of 1648 did not invent sovereignty, they left the Holy Roman Empire in place with its courts and its emperor, and they explicitly gave foreign powers a role as guarantors of the settlement inside the Empire. The idea that 1648 marks a clean break appears to have grown in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, as scholars searched for an origin story for the states system they were describing.

Walking through the town hall of Münster, visitors can still see the Hall of Peace where the Spanish and Dutch envoys swore to their treaty in May 1648, months before the wider settlement was concluded in October. The panelled room is lined with portraits of the delegates, and a glass case holds a gilded cockerel cup from which the town council traditionally drank. Local guides like to point out that the negotiations ran so long that some diplomats raised children in the city. Osnabrück, the second congress town, keeps its own Hall of Peace, and both cities celebrate an annual peace festival in memory of the treaties.

Roman aqueducts carried water from springs and rivers to cities by gravity alone, following a gentle and continuous downward slope over distances that could exceed ninety kilometres. Most of a typical aqueduct ran underground in covered channels cut through rock or built of masonry; the famous arcades were used only where the line had to cross a valley. Engineers surveyed the route with instruments such as the chorobates, a long levelling table, and the groma for straight lines. At the city the water entered a distribution tank and flowed through lead or clay pipes to public fountains, baths and the houses of those who paid for a private connection.

Frontinus, appointed water commissioner of Rome in the year 97, left a short book describing the city's aqueducts and the abuses he found. He complained of illegal taps that diverted water to farms and gardens, of officials who took bribes to look away, and of channel walls left to leak for lack of maintenance. His figures for the capacity of each aqueduct are given in a unit called the quinaria, whose exact volume is still debated, which makes modern estimates of Rome's daily supply vary widely. The text is valuable because it shows the aqueducts as a managed public service with budgets, staff and rules rather than as monuments.

Standing under the Pont du Gard on a hot afternoon, the scale is what strikes you first: three tiers of arches, close to fifty metres high, built without mortar from blocks of local limestone. The bridge carried the aqueduct of Nîmes across the river Gardon, and the whole conduit drops only about twelve metres over some fifty kilometres. Thick deposits of calcium carbonate inside the channel show that it was in use for centuries. Today a footpath crosses the lower tier, a museum explains the construction with full-size models of cranes and scaffolding, and in summer people swim in the river beneath the arches.

Sourdough bread rises because of a community of wild yeasts and lactic acid bacteria living in a starter of flour and water. The yeasts produce carbon dioxide that inflates the dough, while the bacteria make lactic and acetic acids that give the bread its tang and help it keep longer. A starter is fed regularly with fresh flour and water to keep the microbes active; it is ready to use when it doubles in volume a few hours after feeding. Because wild fermentation is slower than baker's yeast, a sourdough loaf usually needs a long bulk rise, often several hours at room temperature or overnight in the refrigerator.

The first three loaves I baked were dense enough to use as doorstops. What changed things was learning to read the dough instead of the clock. My kitchen is cold in winter, so the bulk ferment that the recipe promised would take four hours actually needed seven. Now I watch for the dough to grow by about half, feel airy and jiggle when the bowl is shaken, and show bubbles along the sides. A poke test before baking helps too: if the dent springs back slowly and only partly, the loaf is ready. Baking in a preheated cast iron pot with the lid on for the first twenty minutes gave me a proper crust.

Bakers describe dough by its hydration, the weight of water as a percentage of the weight of flour. A dough of 1000 grams of flour and 700 grams of water is at seventy percent hydration. Higher hydration produces a more open crumb with larger holes but makes the dough slack and sticky to handle. Flour type changes the picture: whole wheat and rye absorb more water than white bread flour, so the same percentage feels stiffer. Salt is usually two percent of the flour weight. Expressing recipes this way, known as baker's percentages, makes it easy to scale a formula up or down and to compare recipes from different sources.

Undercooked chicken is a common source of food poisoning because raw poultry often carries Salmonella and Campylobacter bacteria. The safest way to know that chicken is cooked is to measure its internal temperature with a food thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the meat, away from the bone. Food safety agencies in the United States advise cooking all poultry, including ground poultry, to an internal temperature of 165 degrees Fahrenheit, or 74 degrees Celsius. Colour is not a reliable guide, since meat can stay pink when fully cooked or turn white before it is safe. Leftovers should be refrigerated within two hours and reheated to the same temperature.

Professional cooks often pull chicken breasts from the heat well below the official figure and still serve them safely. The reason is that killing bacteria depends on both temperature and time. At 165 degrees the reduction is practically instant, but holding the meat at 150 degrees for about three minutes achieves the same level of safety, and the breast stays juicier. This is why sous vide recipes cook chicken at lower temperatures for longer periods. The approach requires an accurate thermometer and careful timing, and for home cooks without that equipment the simple single-number rule remains the easier and safer recommendation.

Rinsing raw chicken under the tap is a habit many of us learned from our parents, but it spreads bacteria rather than removing them. Droplets of water splash from the meat onto the sink, the counter and nearby dishes, sometimes more than half a metre away. Cooking kills the bacteria on the surface of the chicken anyway, so washing adds risk without any benefit. Instead, take the chicken straight from the package to the pan, use a separate cutting board for raw meat, and wash your hands with soap after handling it. Any marinade that touched raw poultry should be boiled before it is used as a sauce.

Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy stored in sugars. In plants it takes place in chloroplasts, organelles that contain the green pigment chlorophyll. The process has two linked stages. In the light-dependent reactions, which occur in the thylakoid membranes, light splits water molecules, releasing oxygen and producing the energy carriers ATP and NADPH. In the Calvin cycle, which runs in the surrounding stroma, the enzyme RuBisCO fixes carbon dioxide from the air, and ATP and NADPH power its reduction into three-carbon sugars. These sugars are used to build glucose, sucrose, starch and cellulose, and they feed nearly every food chain on Earth.

RuBisCO is famously inefficient. Besides fixing carbon dioxide, it also reacts with oxygen, starting a wasteful process called photorespiration that releases carbon the plant has already captured. The problem worsens in hot, dry conditions, when leaves close their pores to save water and oxygen builds up inside. Some plants evolved workarounds. C4 plants such as maize and sugarcane first capture carbon dioxide in a four-carbon compound in one cell type and release it next to RuBisCO in another, keeping the enzyme saturated. CAM plants such as cacti open their pores only at night, store the carbon as acid, and photosynthesise with closed pores during the day.

In our classroom experiment, students placed sprigs of pondweed in test tubes of water under a desk lamp and counted the bubbles rising from the cut stems each minute. Moving the lamp closer increased the count, until at the nearest distance the rate stopped climbing, which led to a good discussion about limiting factors. Adding a pinch of sodium bicarbonate to supply more carbon dioxide raised the rate again. Several groups noticed that the lamp also warmed the water, so the next week they repeated the experiment with a beaker of water between the lamp and the tube as a heat shield, and their results became much more consistent.

Le module asyncio de Python exécute des coroutines sur une boucle d'événements à un seul fil. Une coroutine se déclare avec async def et se suspend à chaque expression await, rendant la main à la boucle pour qu'une autre tâche puisse avancer. Comme une seule tâche s'exécute à la fois, asyncio convient aux programmes qui passent l'essentiel de leur temps à attendre des sockets, des tubes ou des minuteries plutôt qu'à calculer. Un travail coûteux en calcul bloque toujours la boucle ; la documentation conseille de le confier à un groupe de fils ou de processus avec run_in_executor. Les tâches se créent avec asyncio.create_task, et asyncio.gather attend plusieurs d'entre elles en rassemblant leurs résultats dans l'ordre.

HTTP-Caches entscheiden anhand des Headers Cache-Control, ob eine gespeicherte Antwort wiederverwendet werden darf. Die Direktive max-age gibt an, wie viele Sekunden eine Antwort frisch bleibt; danach muss der Cache sie beim Ursprungsserver neu validieren, bevor er sie wieder ausliefert. Die Validierung ist günstig, wenn die Antwort einen Validator enthielt. Ein ETag ist eine undurchsichtige Versionskennung, und eine bedingte Anfrage mit If-None-Match erlaubt dem Server, mit 304 Not Modified zu antworten, ohne den Inhalt erneut zu senden. Die Direktive no-store verbietet das Speichern ganz, während no-cache das Speichern erlaubt, aber bei jeder Verwendung eine Validierung verlangt.

La presión arterial alta rara vez causa síntomas, por eso a menudo solo se descubre en un control de rutina. Una medición tiene dos cifras: la presión sistólica mientras el corazón late y la diastólica entre latidos. Muchas guías definen la hipertensión como una lectura sostenida de 140 sobre 90 milímetros de mercurio o más, aunque algunas bajan el umbral a 130 sobre 80. El diagnóstico debe basarse en varias mediciones tomadas en días distintos, idealmente incluyendo mediciones en casa, porque un único valor alto en la consulta puede reflejar ansiedad. Sin tratamiento, la presión elevada daña las arterias durante años y aumenta el riesgo de ictus, infarto y enfermedad renal.

L'article 17 du règlement général sur la protection des données donne à une personne le droit d'obtenir l'effacement, dans les meilleurs délais, de données à caractère personnel la concernant. Ce droit s'applique pour des motifs précis, parmi lesquels le fait que les données ne sont plus nécessaires au regard des finalités pour lesquelles elles ont été collectées, le retrait du consentement sur lequel reposait le traitement, ou un traitement illicite. Il n'est pas absolu. Le responsable du traitement peut refuser l'effacement lorsque le traitement est nécessaire à la liberté d'expression, au respect d'une obligation légale, pour des motifs de santé publique, à des fins d'archivage dans l'intérêt public ou à la défense de droits en justice.

Sauerteigbrot geht auf, weil in einem Ansatz aus Mehl und Wasser eine Gemeinschaft wilder Hefen und Milchsäurebakterien lebt. Die Hefen erzeugen Kohlendioxid, das den Teig aufbläht, während die Bakterien Milch- und Essigsäure bilden, die dem Brot seine Säure geben und es länger haltbar machen. Der Ansatz wird regelmäßig mit frischem Mehl und Wasser gefüttert, damit die Mikroben aktiv bleiben; er ist einsatzbereit, wenn er sich einige Stunden nach dem Füttern im Volumen verdoppelt. Weil die wilde Gärung langsamer ist als Backhefe, braucht ein Sauerteiglaib meist eine lange Stockgare, oft mehrere Stunden bei Raumtemperatur oder über Nacht im Kühlschrank.

La fotosíntesis convierte la energía de la luz en energía química almacenada en azúcares. En las plantas tiene lugar en los cloroplastos, orgánulos que contienen el pigmento verde clorofila. El proceso tiene dos etapas enlazadas. En las reacciones dependientes de la luz, que ocurren en las membranas de los tilacoides, la luz rompe moléculas de agua, libera oxígeno y produce los transportadores de energía ATP y NADPH. En el ciclo de Calvin, que transcurre en el estroma que los rodea, la enzima RuBisCO fija el dióxido de carbono del aire, y el ATP y el NADPH impulsan su reducción a azúcares de tres carbonos, con los que se construyen glucosa, sacarosa, almidón y celulosa.

茶树原产于中国西南地区，早在唐代以前人们就已经开始饮茶。唐代陆羽撰写的《茶经》系统地记述了茶的起源、种植、采摘、制作和煎煮方法，被后人视为世界上第一部茶学专著。宋代流行点茶，人们把茶叶碾成细末，用沸水冲点并以茶筅击拂，使茶汤表面形成细密的泡沫。明代以后，散茶冲泡逐渐取代了团茶和末茶，这种饮法一直延续到今天。按照加工方法的不同，中国茶通常分为绿茶、白茶、黄茶、青茶、红茶和黑茶六大类，各类茶的发酵程度和风味差别很大。
第一次去福建武夷山的茶园，我才明白岩茶为什么叫岩茶。茶树长在峡谷两侧的岩石缝隙里，土壤很薄，矿物质却很丰富。茶农告诉我，采下的鲜叶要先晒青、摇青，让叶片边缘慢慢变红，再经过炒青、揉捻和长时间的炭火烘焙。焙火的轻重决定了茶汤的香气，焙得重的茶带着明显的焦糖和果木味。晚上我们围着小炉子用盖碗冲泡，一泡接一泡，到了第七八泡依然有回甘。离开的时候，我买了两罐大红袍，打算带回去和家人分享。

中国高速铁路网络在过去二十年里迅速扩张，目前运营里程已经位居世界第一。高铁线路一般采用无砟轨道，以减少维护工作量并保证列车在高速运行时的平稳性。复兴号动车组的最高运营速度可以达到每小时三百五十公里，车厢内设有无线网络和充电插座。为了缩短换乘时间，许多大城市把高铁站与地铁和公交枢纽连接在一起。高铁的普及改变了人们的出行方式，过去需要一整天的旅程，现在往往几个小时就能完成，城市之间的联系也因此变得更加紧密。

日本の茶の湯は、室町時代から安土桃山時代にかけて村田珠光、武野紹鴎、千利休らによって形づくられた。利休は狭い草庵の茶室と簡素な道具を好み、侘びの美意識を茶の湯の中心に据えた。亭主は客を迎える前に露地を掃き清め、季節に合わせて掛け物や花を選ぶ。客はにじり口から身をかがめて茶室に入り、身分の差を忘れて一つの空間を共にする。濃茶は一つの茶碗を客同士で回して飲み、薄茶は一人ずつ点てて出される。こうした作法は、もてなす側ともてなされる側の心の通い合いを大切にする考え方から生まれた。

静岡の茶畑を訪ねたのは五月の初め、ちょうど一番茶の摘み取りが始まった頃だった。斜面に整然と並ぶ茶の木の列は、上から見ると緑の縞模様のように見える。農家の方の話では、摘んだ葉はすぐに蒸して酸化を止め、揉みながら乾燥させることで煎茶になるという。工場では大きな機械が休みなく動き、蒸気と青い香りが建物の中に満ちていた。帰り道に立ち寄った茶店で新茶を淹れてもらうと、低めの温度のお湯で出したお茶は甘みが強く、渋みはほとんど感じられなかった。

東海道新幹線は一九六四年、東京オリンピックの開幕直前に東京と新大阪の間で開業した。専用の標準軌の線路を走ることで、在来線では難しかった高速運転を実現した。開業当初の最高速度は時速二百十キロだったが、車両と設備の改良を重ねて現在は時速二百八十五キロで運転している。地震の初期微動を検知して列車を自動的に減速させる仕組みも早くから導入された。数分間隔で列車が発着する過密ダイヤを、平均遅延が一分に満たない正確さで運行していることは、世界の鉄道関係者からも注目されている。

commentary: Editor's note: we are republishing this piece with permission because readers kept asking us the same questions in the comments. Our own view is a little more cautious than the author's, and we want to add some context from our side before you read on. Over the past year our team has tested several of the approaches described below in our own projects, with mixed results. Some advice held up very well, while other parts needed adjustment for our particular situation and budget. We encourage you to read the original critically and to compare it with other sources before you change anything important.

A few readers wrote to point out that the situation is not the same everywhere, and they are right. Regulations, equipment and habits differ between countries and even between neighbouring towns, so treat the details above as one example rather than a universal rule. If you have had a different experience, we would genuinely like to hear about it. We collect the most useful replies and publish a follow-up roundup every few months, crediting everyone who contributed. Thanks to everyone who has already shared their stories, corrections and photographs with us over the years.

Why are we sharing this now? Partly because the topic keeps coming up in our weekly meetings, and partly because the original article explains it more clearly than anything we could have written ourselves. We have added headings, fixed a few broken links and translated some terms for our audience, but otherwise left the text exactly as it was. Below the article you will find a short list of further reading that our editors selected, along with a summary of the discussion that followed when we first posted the link on our forum last spring.

This post is part of our weekly digest, in which we pick one article from elsewhere on the web and add our own commentary for members. Membership pays for the time our editors spend reading dozens of candidates every week to find the one worth your attention. If you enjoyed this selection, consider forwarding the digest to a friend or colleague who might like it too. Next week we will look at a related question from a completely different angle, with an interview that we recorded during our annual meeting in the autumn.

Our take: the core argument is sound, but the piece leaves out costs that matter to small teams and households. Time is the obvious one, followed by the learning curve and the risk of getting the details wrong the first few times. We would also have liked to see more numbers, since anecdotes only go so far when you are deciding where to spend limited money and attention. Still, as an introduction it does its job well, and the practical tips at the end are worth bookmarking for later reference.

Discussion summary: about two hundred members replied when we posted this, and the replies fell into three camps. The first group agreed and added their own examples. The second group thought the explanation was correct but oversimplified for beginners. The third group raised edge cases the article does not cover, several of which our moderators have collected in a pinned thread. We have tried to represent all three views fairly here, and we have linked the full thread for anyone who wants to read every reply in its original form.
